ev_charger.title: EV Charger
ev_charger.description:
SEM auto-detected your EV charger from the Home Assistant entity registry. Review the entries below and click **Submit** — there is usually nothing to change. Optional fields can be left blank.

Pick ONE control path: either a Number Entity (Wallbox, go-eCharger, Heidelberg, OpenWB, Ohme, V2C, …) OR a Service Call (KEBA, Easee, Zaptec, OCPP, …).

data.ev_connected_sensor: 🔌 EV Connected Status — vehicle plug connection
data.ev_charging_sensor: ⚡ EV Charging Active — current charging state
data.ev_charging_power_sensor: 🚗 EV Charging Power — power delivered to vehicle (W)
data.ev_current_control_entity: Number Entity for Current Control (Wallbox-style chargers)
data.ev_total_energy_sensor: 🔋 EV Total Energy — cumulative energy delivered (kWh)

data_description.ev_connected_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether the vehicle plug is currently connected. Auto-detected from KEBA / Easee / Wallbox / go-eCharger / Zaptec / ChargePoint / Heidelberg.
data_description.ev_charging_sensor: Binary sensor that reports whether SEM should consider charging active. Auto-detected from your charger integration.
data_description.ev_charging_power_sensor: Numeric sensor (W) reporting how much power is currently flowing into the vehicle. Auto-detected from your charger integration.
data_description.ev_current_control_entity: Number entity SEM writes to so it can change the charging current (e.g. number.wallbox_charging_current). Use this for chargers that expose a number entity instead of a service call. Leave blank if you fill in the Service path below.
data_description.ev_charger_service: Home Assistant service called to set the charging current (e.g. keba.set_current, easee.set_charger_max_limit). Auto-filled for KEBA. Leave blank if you fill in the Number Entity path above.
data_description.ev_charger_service_entity_id: Entity ID passed as the target of the service call. Auto-filled when needed; leave blank if the service is global.
data_description.ev_current_sensor: Optional. Numeric sensor (A) reporting the actual charging current. Used for diagnostics.
data_description.ev_total_energy_sensor: Optional. Cumulative kWh counter for energy delivered to the vehicle. Used for accurate session tracking.

data.min_solar_power: Minimum solar power — raw PV production (W)

data_description.update_interval: How often the coordinator reads sensors and adjusts hardware. 10 s gives the most accurate energy integration; values above 30 s will under-count energy. Range 10–60 s.
data_description.battery_priority_soc: Zone 1 → Zone 2 boundary. Below this SOC all solar goes to the battery and the EV is blocked. Default 30 %. The four-zone strategy (Architecture docs) needs this LOW (5–60 %) — do NOT confuse with the legacy 3-zone meaning where this was a high target.
data_description.battery_buffer_soc: Zone 2 → Zone 3 boundary. Above this SOC the battery may discharge to bridge solar deficits while charging the EV. Default 70 %.
data_description.battery_auto_start_soc: Zone 3 → Zone 4 boundary. Above this SOC the EV can start charging even with no solar surplus, drawing from the battery. Default 90 %.
data_description.min_solar_power: Raw PV-production floor — the panel output below which 'solar is up' is false: solar_only won't start and the deep-deficit guard treats it as darkness (so charging stops quickly instead of bridging on grid). This is RAW production, NOT surplus — contrast 'Battery assist minimum solar surplus' (solar − home), which decides when the home battery may help. Default 1000 W; keep below the EV charger's hardware minimum (~4140 W 3-phase, ~1380 W 1-phase).
data_description.daily_ev_target: Target kWh per day for night-grid charging. Set to 0 to disable night charging entirely.
data_description.battery_assist_max_power: Maximum power the home battery can discharge to assist the EV in Zone 3/4. Default 4500 W.
data_description.battery_assist_min_surplus: Minimum real solar surplus before the home battery may help charge the EV — in any charging mode. Below this the battery is reserved for the house (the car draws from grid + solar). Default 1200 W. Set to 0 to let the battery support the EV everywhere, including overnight.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable home battery capacity (NOT the EV battery — that's a separate field on the EV step). Used by the forecast-driven charging strategy.
data_description.battery_discharge_protection_enabled: When ON, SEM caps the inverter's discharge limit during night EV charging so the home battery only powers the house (not the EV).
data_description.battery_max_discharge_power: Hard upper limit on battery discharge enforced by the protection feature.
data_description.electricity_import_rate: Day / flat tariff (CHF/kWh, incl. VAT). Used for cost tracking.
data_description.electricity_off_peak_rate: Off-peak rate (per kWh). Set equal to import rate if you don't have a dual tariff.
data_description.electricity_export_rate: Feed-in rate paid by the utility (CHF/kWh).
data_description.demand_charge_rate: Monthly demand charge per kW of peak (CHF/kW/month). Set to 0 if your contract has no demand charge.
data_description.observer_mode: When ON, SEM monitors and calculates everything but never sends a service call to hardware. Use on a test/staging HA mirroring a production install.
data_description.smart_night_charging: When ON, SEM intelligently skips or reduces night charging based on estimated EV SOC, solar forecast, temperature-adjusted consumption prediction, and learned driving patterns.
data_description.battery_discharge_control_entity: Number entity that controls the inverter's discharge power limit (e.g. number.batteries_maximale_entladeleistung on Huawei). Auto-detected on install; override here if needed.
data_description.diagram_style: Choose which system diagram card to use on the Home tab. 'SEM' uses the built-in animated diagram. 'K-Flow' uses the K-Flow HACS card (must be installed separately). Re-run generate_dashboard after changing.
data_description.hot_water_solar_target: Target temperature (°C) for solar-assisted hot water heating. SEM boosts the boiler when surplus is available.
data_description.legionella_target_temp: Temperature (°C) the hot water system must reach during a legionella disinfection cycle.
data_description.legionella_interval_hours: Maximum hours between legionella disinfection cycles before SEM forces a heat-up.

pv_naming.title: Name your PV strings

heat_pump.title: Heat Pump
heat_pump.description:
Configure your heat pump for solar surplus boost. Two control paths are supported:
• **SG-Ready** — set both relay entities (Viessmann, Stiebel Eltron, Vaillant).
• **Climate-only** — set just the climate entity (Nibe, Mitsubishi, Daikin and any HA-controlled heat pump without SG-Ready relays).
Both paths can also be combined. Leave all empty to skip.

data_description.heat_pump_relay1_entity: Switch entity for SG-Ready relay 1 (normal operation signal). Set together with relay 2 for SG-Ready protocol.
data_description.heat_pump_relay2_entity: Switch entity for SG-Ready relay 2 (surplus boost signal). Set together with relay 1 for SG-Ready protocol.
data_description.heat_pump_invert_sg_ready: Enable only if your heat pump's SG-Ready contacts are wired normally-closed (NC). SEM drives the standard SG-Ready truth table; if boost blocks the pump (and vice-versa), turn this on to flip both relays.
data_description.heat_pump_climate_entity: Climate entity used to raise the setpoint during solar surplus. Sufficient on its own for climate-only mode (no relays needed).
data_description.heat_pump_power_sensor: Optional sensor (W) reporting the heat pump's current power consumption.
data_description.heat_pump_boost_offset: Degrees Celsius added to the normal setpoint during a solar surplus boost.
data_description.heat_pump_max_setpoint: Upper temperature limit (°C) SEM will set during a boost cycle.
data_description.heat_pump_priority: Surplus distribution priority relative to other devices. Lower numbers are served first.

ev_charger_not_configured.title: EV charger not configured
ev_charger_not_configured.description: No EV charger sensors are configured, so EV charging features are unavailable. Add an EV “connected” sensor or a charging-power sensor in the integration options to enable EV charging.

sensor_unavailable.title: Sensor unavailable
sensor_unavailable.description: The sensor `{entity_id}` ({friendly_name}) has been unavailable for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM cannot include it in calculations until it recovers. Check the upstream integration (Huawei modbus / Solcast / Forecast.Solar / your inverter network). This issue clears automatically when the sensor next reports a valid value.

sensor_stale.title: Sensor frozen
sensor_stale.description: The sensor `{entity_id}` ({friendly_name}) still reports as available but has not updated in {minutes}+ minutes — it appears frozen. SEM is using its stale value in the energy balance and sign detection, which can distort your figures. Check the upstream integration (Huawei modbus / Growatt cloud / your inverter network). This issue clears automatically when the sensor next updates.

charger_actuation_failed.title: EV charger not accepting commands: {name}
charger_actuation_failed.description: SEM's last 3+ current commands to **{name}** were rejected: `{error}`. The charger is NOT under SEM control right now — it will keep doing whatever it was last told (including charging at full power in off mode). Most common causes: the charger's control entity was renamed by an upstream integration update, or `ev_charger_service` points at a service with a different parameter schema. Check the charger's control entity / service in the SEM config. This issue clears automatically on the next successful command.

no_forecast_integration.title: No solar forecast integration detected
no_forecast_integration.description: SEM looked for a solar-forecast integration (Forecast.Solar, Solcast PV Solar, or a custom forecast sensor) for an hour after startup and didn't find one. Forecast-aware features (best-surplus-window tips, smart night charging, forecast dampening) are inactive until you install one. The issue clears automatically when SEM detects a forecast integration.

no_recorder.title: Recorder integration unavailable
no_recorder.description: SEM tried to bootstrap EV / charging history from the HA recorder but the read failed. EV intelligence (estimated SOC, daily decay) cannot warm-start without it; values populate slowly from live cycles instead. Usually a one-off transient — clears automatically on the next successful recorder read.

heat_pump_relay_unavailable.title: Heat pump SG-Ready {slot} unavailable
heat_pump_relay_unavailable.description: The configured SG-Ready relay entity `{entity_id}` ({slot}) has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM can register the heat pump controller fine, but every SG-Ready command will silently no-op until this entity reports a real state. Check the upstream device — ESP relay board, Shelly, Modbus-bridged template switch, or whichever integration owns this entity. The issue clears automatically when the relay next reports an on/off state.

heat_pump_partial_sg_ready.title: Heat pump SG-Ready half-configured
heat_pump_partial_sg_ready.description: Exactly one of the two SG-Ready relays (`heat_pump_relay1_entity` / `heat_pump_relay2_entity`) is set in SEM, with no climate-entity fallback. The SG-Ready protocol encodes the four states (BLOCKED / NORMAL / BOOST / FORCE_ON) as a 2-bit binary across BOTH relays, so a single relay cannot drive the protocol. Either configure the second relay too, or set a `heat_pump_climate_entity` to use the climate-only setpoint-boost path instead. The issue clears automatically once the config is valid.

hot_water_entity_unavailable.title: Hot water boiler control unavailable
hot_water_entity_unavailable.description: The configured hot-water control entity `{entity_id}` has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM can register the controller fine, but every surplus-dispatch command will silently no-op until the entity reports a real state. Check the upstream device — the boiler relay, water_heater integration, climate device, or whichever integration owns this entity. The issue clears automatically when the entity recovers.

hot_water_temperature_sensor_unavailable.title: Hot water temperature sensor unavailable
hot_water_temperature_sensor_unavailable.description: The configured hot-water temperature sensor `{entity_id}` has been unavailable/unknown for {minutes}+ minutes. SEM fails safe when this sensor is broken — the boiler is NOT activated on surplus until a real temperature reading returns, to avoid running the heater past its target without feedback. Check the sensor's upstream integration. The issue clears automatically when the sensor recovers.

keba_failsafe_active.title: KEBA failsafe is enabled — disable it for steady charging
keba_failsafe_active.description:
Your KEBA charger "{name}" has its failsafe watchdog enabled. SEM (like evcc) no longer relies on it, but while it's on the charger keeps dropping the offered current to its 6 A fallback between commands, which makes charging oscillate (6↔9 A) and some cars (e.g. Renault Zoe) refuse to charge steadily.

Home Assistant's KEBA service can't switch it off (it won't accept a timeout of 0), so you need to disable it at the charger itself: set the **failsafe timeout to 0** (KEBA UDP `failsafe 0 0 1`, or via KEBA's KeContact tooling). See the linked guide for step-by-step instructions. This Repair clears automatically once the failsafe is off.

soc_cap_unenforceable.title: Can't enforce the {target}% charge limit: {name}
soc_cap_unenforceable.description:
**{name}** is set to a percentage charge target, but your vehicle isn't reporting its state of charge right now, so SEM can't stop at **{target}%** — it will keep charging until the car itself tapers (near full).

If your dashboard shows a battery %, that's SEM's *estimated* SOC, which it deliberately ignores for the hard limit (it can drift). To enforce the cap, wire a **real vehicle SOC sensor** for this charger (Configuration → EV → Vehicle SOC entity). This repair clears automatically as soon as a real SOC reading is available again.
